sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Best guide and build for Roccia from WW (Wuthering Waves). Roccia is a 5 ★ rarity character from the Havoc element who uses the Gauntlets type weapon.
 Roccia is a gifted improvisational comedian and the First Mate of the Fool's Troupe, known for her mastery of stage props. With a tranquil, composed disposition, she navigates the ship's quarters, perched atop her giant box, meticulously ensuring the Troupe remains orderly and tidy.

 To learn more about Roccia check the sections below. Use the tabs to quickly switch to the kind of information you're looking for.

sections.heading: Pros
sections.text:
Has a grouping utility that counts as an extra Echo Skill cast.

 Has one of the best JP VAs and the cutest pet known to mankind.

sections.heading: Cons
sections.text:
Outclassed in every team she’s a part of (by Lynae, Qiuyuan or Lucilla), and easily replaced by 4-stars in every team she’s a part of (either by Danjin or Sanhua), particularly without her Signature weapon, where she’s just worse than 4-stars outright.

 Low headroom for Swap Cancels due to a short rotation that relies on 3 mid-air moves that need to be chained one after the other following a specific attack (similar to Qiuyuan).

 Signature is theoretically skippable, but she’s so close in value to 4-star characters that she needs it to stand out from them.

 Very inconsistent rotations before S1; again, a similar problem to Qiuyuan where if one of her mid-airs gets interrupted, her rotation slows down massively and this only stops happening at S1 or higher.

sections.heading: Review
sections.text: Roccia is a 5-star Havoc Gauntlets buffer who specializes in buffing Basic/Havoc DMG-dealing characters, with a focus on AoE grouping and the nice feature of having 1 extra Echo Skill cast compared to regular characters. Her rotation is quite fast and features a lot of mid-air action with some decent personal damage and buffing, similar to other characters of the 1.x-early 2.x era.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics & Rotation
sections.text:
Roccia rotates on the principle of getting her Outro off as quickly as possible, like most supports and buffer-type characters. It provides 20% Havoc and 25% Basic DMG Amplification to the next character for 14s or until they are switched out, like most Hybrid Outros. To charge it up quickly, she needs to access some mid-air bouncing Heavy Attacks called “Real Fantasy”, as all stages give a ton of Concerto upon landing, increasing as the chain goes on.
 To cast them, she needs to use (and hence build up) Imagination, her Forte gauge split in 3 bars. Roccia can achieve this either by charging a Heavy Attack on the ground, which is rather slow (but at least not slower than most of her Basics), or rotate with an Intro (which chains into a Basic 4) and a Skill, each restoring one of the thirds, which is much faster. Her Skill and ground Heavy Attack are in fact the only ways Roccia has of casting her Real Fantasy bounces, so in case she gets interrupted, her Heavy Attack is your best bet. This will however, slow Roccia’s rotation down significantly and is often grounds for resetting an endgame content run.
 Her Ultimate also buffs the whole party’s ATK by up to 200 for 30s based on her CRIT Rate (maxxing out at 70%) upon casting. And upon casting Outro, Roccia unlocks a special Utility called Magic Box (like the Grapple, Flight or Motorbike utilities, for example), which counts as an extra Echo Skill cast. It deals a flat 100 damage but can group small enemies with your incoming character while Roccia is off-field.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
sections.text:
As you can see, we’re already done explaining all of Roccia’s buffs and essential rotation moves; she’s an extremely simple character. But that’s unfortunately not to her benefit. In the short rotation, Basic DMG buffing department, Sanhua is an extremely obvious pick that at S6 is already rivaling Roccia for her one use in Basic DMG buffing: Camellya. She already had a fully constituted team with Sanhua, and unfortunately for Roccia - who takes longer to rotate than the fastest Hybrid character in the entire game - her higher personal damage does not justify the rotation time increase, not to mention her buffs are barely better than Sanhua’s for Camellya specifically (and in terms of Basic DMG buffing, that’s all Roccia’s good at). To make matters worse, her grouping is not necessary since Camellya already has some of the widest AoE attacks in the entire game with her spin, Ultimate and Forte Skill. Overall, regarding her Outro and grouping, Roccia only exists as a sidegrade to a completely free character. Not looking good there.
 So let’s shift the focus over to her personal damage and extra Echo Skill cast. She’s a perfect fit for the Phrolova team: an ideal recipient for Phrolova’s Outro, a party-wide ATK buff with her Ultimate, an extra Echo Skill cast to trigger an enhanced Hecate attack. Sure, her grouping is again not needed, since Hecate is the best crowd control utility in the entire game to date, but surely this makes Roccia good, right? Again, a missed opportunity. She’s barely better than Danjin, not better than Shorekeeper, and definitely way worse than Qiuyuan and Lucilla.
 And this unfortunately already exhausted Roccia’s 2 “best” meta niches, if you can even call them that. Even with her Signature weapon equipped, Roccia’s personal damage increases barely make her better than her 4-star competition. In conclusion, Roccia, since her release, has always been destined to fail. She never stood out, even in 2 teams that were built with her in mind, due to a lack of significant buffs and not enough unique features compared to the free alternatives Sanhua and Danjin, and stronger premium alternatives like Lynae (for Camellya) and Qiuyuan/Lucilla (for Phrolova). Overall, unless you’re willing to pull Sequences for Roccia (which in itself is not even an optimal choice since you rather get Sequences on the DPS characters she supports or universal 3rd slots instead), unfortunately she’s either a sidegrade to free characters at best, or a bad premium alternative at worst, making her one of the least valuable limited 5-stars in Wuthering Waves. Here’s to hoping for a Roccia kit buff, because she needs one.

 ATK, CRIT Rate and DMG Bonus stat-stick for Roccia, who does not benefit from this weapon's Liberation DMG-related effects.

 Best permanent banner option, grants Roccia some much-desired 24% CRIT Rate and a strong Base ATK to work with. Good stat-stick without any extra effects.
 84.70%

 Massive CRIT Rate stat-stick at the cost of lower Base ATK, Roccia does not benefit from this weapon's Liberation DMG-related effects though.

 Second best permanent weapon option, grants Roccia some Energy Regen and a lot of ATK%, but CRIT Rate requirements will be difficult to hit and the DMG Bonus effects are practically useless on her.
 72.90%

 Aether Strike (R 5 )

 This Battle Pass exclusive grants Roccia some CRIT DMG and easily accessed ATK bonuses, making it the overall best 4-star choice theoretically. Still, meeting CRIT Rate requirements will prove difficult and this weapon is overall not recommended over Pulsation Bracer or her Signature, like any other 4-star, due to their lower Base ATK.
 72.60%

 Celestial Spiral (R 5 )

 Grants Roccia some flat Energy to alleviate Energy requirements and a decent Base ATK, but is just an ATK stat-stick beyond this with nothing much to provide Roccia with.
 69.50%

 Stonard (R 5 )

 This Battle Pass exclusive has a useless Liberation DMG-boosting passive for Roccia, but provides her with some CRIT Rate to alleviate her requirements there. Still not recommended though, due to low Base ATK and generally bad stats.
 69.20%

 Hollow Mirage (R 5 )

 Simple ATK stat-stick that relies on you not getting hit to leverage its ATK-boosting passive stacks fully. Not recommended on Roccia, like any other 4-star weapon.
 66.60%

 Legend of Drunken Hero (R 5 )

 Best no-gacha option for Roccia, simple ATK stat-stick with no passive to take advantage of whatsoever since it's Negative Status-related and Roccia plays in no such teams. This can be a temporary weapon choice, but to move away from this weapon and equip her with at least Pulsation Bracer as soon as possible, if you can.

sections.heading: Best Echo Sets
sections.text:
1

Midnight Veil

 Offers a 10% unconditional Havoc DMG% boost alongside adding a large Havoc Damage hit to the Outro of the wearer. Also grants the incoming resonator a Havoc DMG% boost when the wearer uses their Outro. The set is better than Moonlit Clouds if and only if the equipped character's Echoes have endgame investment (with 9 or 10 CRIT substats total) and the character has a 5-star weapon equipped. If both conditions aren't met, Moonlit Clouds is a better choice.
 Below you can find Main Echo options:

 Nightmare: Impermanence Heron

 - Offers an unconditional 12% Havoc DMG and 12% Heavy Attack DMG boost when placed in the Main Echo slot, making it a solid choice for Havoc focused resonators who emphasize Heavy Attack damage and are looking to use the 5P Midnight Veil set bonus.

 2

Moonlit Clouds

 Offers a 10% unconditional Energy Regen% boost taking some pressure off your gear when aiming at ER breakpoints. Also upon using Outro, grants the next character switching in a 22.5% ATK boost, amplifying any of your main damage dealers burst windows.
 Below you can find Main Echo options:

 Impermanence Heron

 - Supportive Echo that can be run at the cost of a sizeable chunk of damage for the character who equips, trading personal gain for team benefits. Should always be used and immediately switch cancelled right before performing an Outro, leading to another DPS. When done so will grant the next character switching in 12% increased DMG% which when combined with the 5P Moonlit set which also grants 22.5% ATK% under the same conditions makes for a sizeable boost. While the echo does lower the damage of whoever wears it, it grants a massive chunk of energy on use usually saving 1 or sometimes even 2 Energy Regen sub stats that may otherwise be needed by the wearer allowing for some damage to be recovered.

sections.heading: Rotation & Gameplay
sections.text:
Roccia’s rotations have very little room for flexibility and (infamously) lots of room for interruption. While she is very easy to play, be careful when rotating with her and keep in mind to dodge enemy attacks during her mid-air bounces.

sections.heading: Echo Timing
sections.text: Varies depending on the rotation, but Roccia always uses a single-cast Transform Echo so timings will be written within the rotation.

sections.heading: Standard Rotation
sections.text:
Intro

 Basic 4 (Cancel animation endlag via Ultimate)

 Ultimate

 Skill (Interrupt animation via Dash on 1st hit)

 Dash

 Basic: Real Fantasy 1

 Basic: Real Fantasy 2

 Basic: Real Fantasy 3 (Cancel animation endlag via Echo)

 Echo (Swap)

 Outro

 Ultimate is used right after Basic 4 to ensure the quickest possible uptime on its ATK buff, as well as making Energy requirements on the 2nd rotation more lenient (in case of missing hits or interruption, for example). Although it’s fine to use it after all 3 Real Fantasies if needed. Skill is Dash Cancelled since it provides little benefit damage-wise; only the Concerto, Forte and Real Fantasy status matter, both being given on cast or by the 1st hit. sections.heading: S6 Main DPS Rotation
sections.text:
Finally, at S6, since Roccia can bounce indefinitely following her Real Fantasy bounces, she can rotate as an effective Main DPS like so:
 Intro

 Basic 4 (Interrupt animation instantly via Ultimate to activate Signature passive)

 Ultimate

 Skill (Interrupt animation via Dash on 1st hit)

 Dash

 Basic: Real Fantasy 1

 Basic: Real Fantasy 2

 Basic: Real Fantasy 3

 Basic: Fantasy Recreation (Until Outro buffs run out, should be up to 9 times) (Swap)

 Outro

 We may skip out on casting Echo in this rotation, since casting an extra Fantasy Recreation Basic and switching out is a much better use of Roccia’s rotation time. Roccia may cast her Echo before her Intro if the team has proper Swap Cancel windows to allow for it.
 Ultimate is cast immediately in spite of her Signature’s passive in order to have a smooth transition into her infinite Fantasy bounces.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
Camellya - Roccia amplifies Havoc DMG by 20% and Basic Attack DMG by 25% on Outro, making the synergy with Camellya, who does those two damage types the most by far, extremely natural. Camellya's best in slot buffer, no doubt (despite being very competitive with Sanhua).
 Phrolova - Roccia is one of the best third slot teammate to the Phrolova-Cantarella trio as she is the best recipient of Phrolova's Outro Skill which amplifies Havoc DMG and Heavy Attack DMG by 20% and 25% respectively, lining up with Roccia's damage types and allowing a trio with Cantarella to always upkeep high damage, making for a strong Phrolova team.
 Rover (Havoc) - Roccia's 20% Havoc and 25% Basic Attack DMG Amplify on Outro are some of the best buffs Havoc Rover can receive, but additionally Roccia's grouping are very much appreciated with Havoc Rover's small AoE attacks that do big damage. Easily Havoc Rover's best buffer.
 Verina - One of the usual Healing Support options that can slot into any team. Super easy to use, provides amazing team-wide ATK% buffs and 15% DMG Amplify with one of the fastest rotations in the game. Enjoy.
 The Shorekeeper - Similar to Verina, a premium Healing Support option who can not only slot into any team, but also provide insane 12.5% Crit Rate, 25% Crit DMG, 25% ATK and 15% DMG Amplify buffs to your whole team. One of the best but also easy to use characters in the game.

 Pros & Cons
 Pros
 Has a grouping utility that counts as an extra Echo Skill cast.

 Has one of the best JP VAs and the cutest pet known to mankind.

 Cons
 Outclassed in every team she’s a part of (by Lynae, Qiuyuan or Lucilla), and easily replaced by 4-stars in every team she’s a part of (either by Danjin or Sanhua), particularly without her Signature weapon, where she’s just worse than 4-stars outright.

 Low headroom for Swap Cancels due to a short rotation that relies on 3 mid-air moves that need to be chained one after the other following a specific attack (similar to Qiuyuan).

 Signature is theoretically skippable, but she’s so close in value to 4-star characters that she needs it to stand out from them.

 Very inconsistent rotations before S1; again, a similar problem to Qiuyuan where if one of her mid-airs gets interrupted, her rotation slows down massively and this only stops happening at S1 or higher.

 Review
 Roccia is a 5-star Havoc Gauntlets buffer who specializes in buffing Basic/Havoc DMG-dealing characters, with a focus on AoE grouping and the nice feature of having 1 extra Echo Skill cast compared to regular characters. Her rotation is quite fast and features a lot of mid-air action with some decent personal damage and buffing, similar to other characters of the 1.x-early 2.x era.
 Key Mechanics & Rotation
 Roccia rotates on the principle of getting her Outro off as quickly as possible, like most supports and buffer-type characters. It provides 20% Havoc and 25% Basic DMG Amplification to the next character for 14s or until they are switched out, like most Hybrid Outros. To charge it up quickly, she needs to access some mid-air bouncing Heavy Attacks called “Real Fantasy”, as all stages give a ton of Concerto upon landing, increasing as the chain goes on.
 To cast them, she needs to use (and hence build up) Imagination, her Forte gauge split in 3 bars. Roccia can achieve this either by charging a Heavy Attack on the ground, which is rather slow (but at least not slower than most of her Basics), or rotate with an Intro (which chains into a Basic 4) and a Skill, each restoring one of the thirds, which is much faster. Her Skill and ground Heavy Attack are in fact the only ways Roccia has of casting her Real Fantasy bounces, so in case she gets interrupted, her Heavy Attack is your best bet. This will however, slow Roccia’s rotation down significantly and is often grounds for resetting an endgame content run.
 Her Ultimate also buffs the whole party’s ATK by up to 200 for 30s based on her CRIT Rate (maxxing out at 70%) upon casting. And upon casting Outro, Roccia unlocks a special Utility called Magic Box (like the Grapple, Flight or Motorbike utilities, for example), which counts as an extra Echo Skill cast. It deals a flat 100 damage but can group small enemies with your incoming character while Roccia is off-field.
 Meta Position & Conclusion
 As you can see, we’re already done explaining all of Roccia’s buffs and essential rotation moves; she’s an extremely simple character. But that’s unfortunately not to her benefit. In the short rotation, Basic DMG buffing department, Sanhua is an extremely obvious pick that at S6 is already rivaling Roccia for her one use in Basic DMG buffing: Camellya. She already had a fully constituted team with Sanhua, and unfortunately for Roccia - who takes longer to rotate than the fastest Hybrid character in the entire game - her higher personal damage does not justify the rotation time increase, not to mention her buffs are barely better than Sanhua’s for Camellya specifically (and in terms of Basic DMG buffing, that’s all Roccia’s good at). To make matters worse, her grouping is not necessary since Camellya already has some of the widest AoE attacks in the entire game with her spin, Ultimate and Forte Skill. Overall, regarding her Outro and grouping, Roccia only exists as a sidegrade to a completely free character. Not looking good there.
 So let’s shift the focus over to her personal damage and extra Echo Skill cast. She’s a perfect fit for the Phrolova team: an ideal recipient for Phrolova’s Outro, a party-wide ATK buff with her Ultimate, an extra Echo Skill cast to trigger an enhanced Hecate attack. Sure, her grouping is again not needed, since Hecate is the best crowd control utility in the entire game to date, but surely this makes Roccia good, right? Again, a missed opportunity. She’s barely better than Danjin, not better than Shorekeeper, and definitely way worse than Qiuyuan and Lucilla.
 And this unfortunately already exhausted Roccia’s 2 “best” meta niches, if you can even call them that. Even with her Signature weapon equipped, Roccia’s personal damage increases barely make her better than her 4-star competition. In conclusion, Roccia, since her release, has always been destined to fail. She never stood out, even in 2 teams that were built with her in mind, due to a lack of significant buffs and not enough unique features compared to the free alternatives Sanhua and Danjin, and stronger premium alternatives like Lynae (for Camellya) and Qiuyuan/Lucilla (for Phrolova). Overall, unless you’re willing to pull Sequences for Roccia (which in itself is not even an optimal choice since you rather get Sequences on the DPS characters she supports or universal 3rd slots instead), unfortunately she’s either a sidegrade to free characters at best, or a bad premium alternative at worst, making her one of the least valuable limited 5-stars in Wuthering Waves. Here’s to hoping for a Roccia kit buff, because she needs one.

 The Shorekeeper - Similar to Verina, a premium Healing Support option who can not only slot into any team, but also provide insane 12.5% Crit Rate, 25% Crit DMG, 25% ATK and 15% DMG Amplify buffs to your whole team. One of the best but also easy to use characters in the game.
